blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (The settlement worker can fail without anyone seeing it) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back until Paylane is proven in production: a configuration switch selecting Stripe or Paylane at runtime (or a gradual rollout behind it), with the Stripe client kept for that period, and the Stripe account kept open until a stated exit criterion is met (e.g. a full settlement cycle with no unmatched payments). Today, if Paylane fails or misbehaves after the release, the operator has no switch, and redeploying the previous version no longer works once the Stripe account is closed the next day: card payments stay down until a new release against a reopened account.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide in the design how an operator sees the worker fail or not run: an alert on a failed or missed CronJob run (e.g. on the time of the last successful run), metrics for payments fetched, matched and unmatched, and a log at start and end of each run. Today, if the Paylane API is down at 02:00 or the job crashes or is never scheduled, no settlement happens and nothing reports it — the finance alert of the spec fires only for unmatched payments of a run that succeeded — so payments go unreconciled for days unnoticed.
findings.title: The settlement worker can fail without anyone seeing it
